To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
users want a chatbot like a friend that is productive, funny, and emotionally expressive.

(1) Users want a bot that adds value to their life; (2) Users want the bot to be fun and friendly; and (3) Users want the chatbot to understand their context and be able to make recommendations based on their needs and preferences.
users wanted a productivity oriented bot that is also a friend, and that they wanted to have some fun with it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of chatbots that are not merely useful, but that are also likeable and preferred.
the personality of a chatbot and the kind of interaction that users are seeking.
understanding the expectations and preferences that young, urban Indian users have of a chatbot.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
users want a chatbot that is a friend and a helper.
users want a bot that is a friend, a companion, and a guide.
users want their chatbot to be Maya, with the personality of Evi, and the fun of Ada.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
users wanted a “Maya with Ada’s personality and Evi’s emotional traits.”
users wanted a “Maya” chatbot with the “Ada” personality.
the chatbot needs to be “human”, but not “human-like”.
The main takeaway from our work is that
users are seeking a balance between the chatbot adding value and being a friend, and that the chatbot should have the ability to adapt to user preferences.
users want a chatbot to be like Maya—a friend that adds value to their life.
chatbot personality is important, but users want to be able to choose the chatbot personality they want.
